scope: Review of the supplied, collected primary evidence; not an exhaustive survey of all publications. This review is limited to the supplied eligible source set and permits one new security-context item from the Premium Times report. The excerpt supports a reported ACLED-based trend in Boko Haram/JAS violence and a caution against over-attributing that decline to a reported ceasefire. The material does not support any new national or zonal public-opinion poll, and it does not provide enough methodology detail for a polling record. Exact incident-level dates, full ACLED tables, and broader corroboration are not available in the supplied evidence.
summary: No material change accepted from the supplied evidence. Published assessments and data dates are unchanged.

security_context.title: Boko Haram violence declines
security_context.summary: Premium Times reports an ACLED-based decline in Boko Haram/JAS violence in Nigeria across 2026, with lower recorded events in the second and third quarters than earlier in the year. The report also notes cross-border activity in Cameroon and Chad and cautions that the decline cannot be attributed solely to the reported ceasefire.
security_context.geography: Nigeria, with regional spillover into Cameroon, Chad and Niger

event_window.note: The article describes ACLED data for the first quarter of 2025 through the third quarter of 2026; exact incident dates are not provided in the excerpt.

verification.method: Independent AI review plus deterministic provenance and schema checks

caveat: Exact citations and hashes establish retrieval and traceability. Independent review assesses interpretation; neither guarantees survey quality. Historical sources and X themes are not revalidated by this check.
